title.narrative: UNFPA CSE out of school phase II

description.narrative:
Norad support CSE Out of school PHASE I 2018-2021 with a no cost extention for 2022. This agreement is the next phase of this programme, with more countries and parters included. The overall goal of PHASE II is: To empower and equip adolescents and young people from specific groups left behind with the information and the skills through out of school CSE, so that they can make informed choices about their sexual and reproductive health and rights, and well-being. The programme has three pillars/outcomes that are the same for phase I and II:
Outcome 1: International guidance on OOS CSE rolled out across countries and regions Outcome 2: Participatory, relevant, and contextualized models of OOS CSE programming established and tested Outcome 3: Evidence, knowledge management and innovation of strategic information, lessons learned and best practices The proposal document lists key research priorities for PHASE II developed by the research partners (p.14). They include: - Understanding which groups of young people are not being reached by school-based CSE and why, and whether they are able to get CSE through other means. - Building functional links and referral pathways between CSE and health and social services. - Identifying where resistance to out-of-school CSE comes from, why, and how to address it.
The target groups will be the same as in the first phase of the project; young, returned migrants, refugees, indigenous young people, young people with disabilities, young female sex workers, LGBTQ+ people, adolescents, and youth at risk of HIV, Young people living with HIV, and young people in detention. This PHASE II of the project intends to scale up CSE out of school efforts in more countries. The main countries are Colombia, Ethiopia, The Philippines, Ghana, Indonesia, Iran, Nicaragua, Nigeria, Malawi, Moldova, Tunisia and Palestine.
